product.problem_statement: Traditional drug development requires months to years of experiments and enormous costs for molecule design. Existing AI models are either less accessible or locked to specific companies.
product.solution: An open-source-based platform allows scientists and AI agents to directly design and optimize molecules. It provides small molecule (BoltzMol-1) and protein (BoltzProt-1) design models, with API and on-premise deployment support.
key_features: BoltzMol-1: small-molecule design model that shortens hit discovery to weeks and cuts costs to as low as $10,000
BoltzProt-1: Protein design model, 3x higher hit rate than BoltzGen, superior to existing models
Blazing-fast inference: Uses thousands of GPUs on demand for design within minutes
Secure deployment: Multi-tenant, single-tenant, and on-premise support, SOC 2 Type 1 certified

product.target_customer: Global pharmaceutical companies (Pfizer, GSK, Takeda, BMS), biotechs, and industrial firms (e.g., DSM Firmenich)
product.business_model: Token-based usage pricing: Charges based on molecule token throughput; customers retain ownership of their creations

direct_competitors.comparison: AI-based drug discovery platform, but relies on large experimental data and closed pipelines
Specializes in AI drug discovery, but focuses on proprietary pipelines rather than open-source approach
Strong in protein structure prediction, but lacks molecule design and optimization capabilities

competitive_landscape.key_differentiator: Open-source-first approach gains trust from the scientific community, offering flexible integration with open models and APIs
competitive_landscape.moat: Open-source model community with over 5 million downloads; references from 6 of the global top 20 pharmaceutical companies as customers
competitive_landscape.competitive_position_summary: A leading open-source platform in biomolecular AI, differentiated by supporting the entire molecule design process in a single workflow.

e2b-2026.tagline: An infrastructure platform that rents dedicated cloud computers to AI agents.

product.summary: E2B is a cloud platform that provides isolated microVM sandboxes in milliseconds, enabling AI agents to safely execute code, manipulate files, browse the web, and more.
product.problem_statement: Traditional infrastructure (Docker, Kubernetes) is designed to run pre-defined software; however, AI agents generate and execute code at runtime, leading to shortcomings in security isolation, fast boot times, and network control.
product.solution: It instantly creates a complete virtual machine per agent session, with built-in file system, browser, network firewall, credential management, etc., enabling agents to use a computer just like a human.
key_features: Isolated microVM (one session per sandbox)
Millisecond boot (restore from snapshot)
Built-in browser and file system
Per-session network firewall and filtering
Observability metrics (pause, fork, getMetrics)
SOC 2 Type II certified, HIPAA compliant
Deployable on E2B Cloud or within customer AWS/GCP/Azure accounts
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: MicroVM-based isolation, open-source sandbox protocol, model/API-agnostic design.
product.target_customer: Enterprises developing or deploying AI agents (88% of Fortune 100 have signed up), especially those requiring large-scale computer use.
product.business_model: Usage-based pricing (based on number of sandbox starts and resource consumption). 100% inbound growth through its own service platform.

direct_competitors.comparison: General-purpose infrastructure like EC2 and Lambda cannot immediately provide agent-specific sandboxing and network isolation. E2B adds an AI-specific layer.
Similar general-purpose cloud, but E2B differentiates with an open-source protocol and network effects; in fact, they have formed a partnership.
Containers have weak security isolation and are unsuitable for dynamic network control of agent-generated code.

competitive_landscape.key_differentiator: Isolated microVM designed from scratch for AI agents + millisecond boot + complete OS environment (browser, file, network) provided via a single API.
competitive_landscape.moat: The open-source sandbox protocol has become the de facto standard (200M+ sandbox starts). Network effects with 94 Fortune 100 companies using it. Building internally would cost $500K+ per year and require 5–10 engineers.
competitive_landscape.competitive_position_summary: First mover in AI agent infrastructure market to achieve enterprise-grade adoption. While cloud big tech competitors are expected to follow, E2B is defending through open-source and partnership strategies.

stepsecurity-2026.tagline: Software supply chain security platform protecting developer environments and CI/CD pipelines

founders.background: He led the Azure Security team at Microsoft for 15 years.
After working at Microsoft for about 8 years, he was responsible for cloud and infrastructure security at Uber and Plaid.

product.summary: A supply chain security platform that protects all environments where software is built, including developer laptops, code repositories, package downloads, and CI/CD pipelines.
product.problem_statement: Supply chain attacks are increasing, where malicious code is inserted into open-source packages or CI/CD pipelines, leading to credential leakage or code tampering. Existing security tools focus on production environments and fail to block attacks during the development phase.
product.solution: Deploys lightweight agents and automated checks at each point—developer machines, code repositories, package registries, and CI/CD runners—so that even if a malicious component passes one layer, it is blocked at another.
key_features: Harden-Runner: Real-time monitoring of processes, network, and file changes using eBPF on CI/CD runners, blocking anomalous behavior.
Dev Machine Guard: Inventories AI coding agents, IDE extensions, and local packages on developer laptops and detects threats.
Secure Registry: Blocks malicious packages from public registries like npm before download, and holds new releases for a certain period.
Repository Checks: Fixes vulnerabilities in repository settings and package dependencies through automated security PRs.
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: Uses eBPF (Extended Berkeley Packet Filter) on CI/CD runners to track process and network behavior at the kernel level. Unlike traditional EDR focused on production, it provides build-environment-specific behavioral analysis.
product.target_customer: Software development and security teams at enterprises using GitHub Actions
product.business_model: Offers subscription pricing at $16 per contributing developer per month (Enterprise), with Harden-Runner free for open-source projects.

direct_competitors.comparison: Raised a $60M Series B in May 2026 at a $1B valuation, focusing on open-source package screening. StepSecurity covers a broader scope with developer environment and CI/CD behavioral analysis.
An incumbent with strengths in enterprise open-source component analysis and vulnerability management. StepSecurity focuses on earlier-stage supply chain security (developer machines, CI/CD).
Provides artifact management and package security within a DevSecOps platform. StepSecurity differentiates by independent developer environment protection.
Offers open-source dependency management and security. StepSecurity provides deeper behavioral analysis in CI/CD runtime protection.

competitive_landscape.key_differentiator: Its build-environment-specific eBPF-based behavioral analysis (Harden-Runner) has been adopted by over 20,000 projects in the open-source community, accumulating early detection cases of real-world attacks.
competitive_landscape.moat: A large user base secured through a free open-source tier and the attack pattern data derived from it make it difficult for latecomers to enter. Additionally, the multi-layer protection architecture covering developer machines, packages, and CI/CD is hard to replicate.
competitive_landscape.competitive_position_summary: Leads the narrow but rapidly growing segment of 'developer environment protection' in the supply chain security market, strengthening its position with 5x consecutive growth. Competes with well-funded rivals (Socket) but differentiates through open-source community presence and behavioral analysis technology.

marrow-therapeutics-2026.tagline: A biotech treating sickle cell disease and beta thalassemia with bone marrow-targeted gene therapy

founders.background: PhD in immunology and microRNA biology (Mount Sinai)

marrow-therapeutics-2026.team_highlights: CEO Romesh Subramanian founded Dyne Therapeutics and RaNA Therapeutics, and led Translate Bio. He has deep experience in antibody-nucleic acid conjugates.

product.summary: Marrow Therapeutics is developing a platform that delivers gene therapies directly to bone marrow cells in vivo for sickle cell disease and beta thalassemia. Using the Transferrin Antibody Bioconjugate (TAB) platform, it delivers siRNA payloads to erythroid progenitor cells in the bone marrow, silencing BCL11A and reactivating fetal hemoglobin production.
product.problem_statement: Currently approved gene therapies (e.g., Vertex's Casgevy) manipulate patient stem cells ex vivo and then reinfuse them. This makes manufacturing very expensive and requires hospital infrastructure, limiting global patient access.
product.solution: Developing an in vivo therapy that can be administered via a single subcutaneous injection. The drug binds to the transferrin receptor (TfR1), enters bone marrow cells without disrupting iron transport, and induces gene silencing.
key_features: Bone marrow-specific delivery via transferrin receptor (TfR1) targeting
siRNA payload targeting BCL11A mRNA
Room temperature stability and self-administered subcutaneous injection formulation
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: The Transferrin Antibody Bioconjugate (TAB) platform is a proprietary structure combining an antibody, small molecule linker, and nucleic acid drug. It selectively binds to highly expressed TfR1 on erythroid progenitor cells to deliver the drug.
product.target_customer: Patients worldwide with sickle cell disease and beta thalassemia
product.business_model: Revenue generation through therapy sales; pricing strategy aligned with global insurance and government payment systems, targeting lower prices and broader accessibility compared to competitors.

direct_competitors.comparison: Casgevy (CRISPR-based ex vivo gene therapy) is approved but limited by manufacturing complexity and high cost. Marrow differentiates with an in vivo approach.
Lyfgenia (ex vivo gene therapy for sickle cell disease) is under development but, unlike Marrow, requires an ex vivo process.

competitive_landscape.key_differentiator: In vivo approach allows treatment with a single injection without stem cell harvesting and reinfusion, enabling manufacturing simplification and cost reduction.
competitive_landscape.moat: The TAB platform is a targeted delivery technology leveraging high TfR1 expression in the bone marrow. A similar approach (Denali Therapeutics' Avlayah) received FDA approval, validating clinical feasibility.
competitive_landscape.competitive_position_summary: Marrow is in preclinical stages but holds a differentiated position with its proprietary delivery technology and large-scale fundraising. While competitors' products are ex vivo, the key is whether Marrow can gain an advantage in accessibility and pricing through its in vivo approach.

trending_reason.summary: On November 17, 2026, it emerged from stealth mode with $173M raised ($53M Series A + $120M Series B) and officially launched. Notable healthcare investors including OrbiMed, Scion Life Sciences, and venBio participated, drawing attention.
catalysts: Large Series B funding ($120M) led by OrbiMed
Preclinical data (monkey studies) for the transferrin receptor-based bone marrow delivery platform confirmed target binding and BCL11A inhibition
FDA approval of Denali Therapeutics' similar mechanism drug (Avlayah) provides technology validation
trending_reason.growth_metrics: No specific growth metrics yet as it has not entered clinical trials.

market_outlook.tam_sam_som: The global market for sickle cell disease and beta thalassemia is estimated at several billion dollars. With Vertex's Casgevy priced at millions of dollars annually, there is significant room for new therapies to enter the market.
market_outlook.market_trend: Following approval of ex vivo gene therapies, demand is growing for in vivo therapies that address accessibility and cost issues. The transferrin receptor-mediated delivery approach has an FDA-approved precedent (DNA), suggesting scalability.
market_outlook.growth_potential: If successful, it could replace a significant portion of the existing ex vivo therapy market, with major growth expected especially in regions lacking medical infrastructure.
risks: Risk of transitioning from preclinical to clinical trials
Need to demonstrate safety and efficacy of in vivo siRNA delivery
Possibility that competitors (e.g., Vertex) also pursue in vivo approaches
Challenges in manufacturing process optimization and cost reduction
market_outlook.risk_mitigation: Monkey studies demonstrated target binding and fetal hemoglobin induction. Management has experience commercializing similar platforms. Transferrin receptor-based delivery technology has already received FDA approval for a separate drug.

marrow-therapeutics-2026.editor_pick_comment: Marrow is betting that transferrin receptor targeting can solve the complexity and cost of ex vivo gene therapy, but in vivo delivery efficacy and safety have yet to be proven in the clinic. It remains to be seen whether we will enter an era of treating genetic diseases with injections instead of blood transfusions.

product.summary: An AI agent service that calls or communicates online with medical institutions, insurers, and pharmacies on behalf of users to handle appointment booking, price comparison for prescriptions, and medical bill disputes.

product.summary: Planet Savers develops an electrically driven direct air capture (DAC) system using zeolite adsorbents. key_features: Proprietary zeolite adsorbent: significantly improved CO₂ adsorption capacity and rate, desorption energy one-third that of chemical adsorption.

Desorption possible with low-temperature waste heat or depressurization only, reducing construction costs.
Adsorbent durability over 10 years, low maintenance costs.

product.summary: Rerun is a multimodal data stack for physical AI (robotics, autonomous driving, drones, spatial computing). It consists of an open-source SDK and a commercial database, Rerun Hub.
product.problem_statement: Existing data tools (such as RViz) were designed before the machine learning era, suitable for online log visualization but not for large-scale offline data processing. Researchers often had to write extensive translation code to reinterpret data at each pipeline stage, leading to slow iteration speed.
product.solution: Rerun provides an integrated data layer that can handle logging, storage, query, transformation, visualization, and training all at once with the same SDK. The open-source Rerun SDK offers Python, C++, and Rust APIs, while Rerun Hub is a commercial backend that supports large-scale cataloging, query, transformation, and training streaming on top of object storage.

Search inside large-scale recordings by column, time range, and value using DataFrames and SQL queries
Built-in MCP server for controlling local AI agents
Direct streaming via byte-range reads on object storage
No need for training-specific exports with a video codec-aware data loader
Enterprise support with single-tenant isolation, S3-compatible storage, SSO, etc.
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: Leverages Rust-based high-performance GUI (egui), Apache DataFusion, and experience with the rosbag format. Designed to support column-level queries and byte indexing while preserving data in its native form.
product.target_customer: Robotics research teams, autonomous driving companies, drone companies, spatial computing/embedded AI startups, and research institutions.
product.business_model: Open-source SDK is free under the MIT license. Rerun Hub is monetized via commercial subscription (cloud or on-premises).

product.summary: AgentOS is an enterprise AI agent operating system that structures data and business rules distributed across multiple systems (SAP, ERP, CRM, etc.) into an ontology, enabling AI agents to reason and execute actual tasks.

key_features: Ontology-based data integration: Structures data and business rules from distributed systems (SAP, ERP, CRM, etc.) in terms of meaning and relationships.

Agent builder: Combines agents, tools, rules, and conditions per task to create custom AI agents.

product.summary: Blinka offers USD checking accounts, global transfers, Visa Infinite corporate cards, and short-term treasury management (T-bill MMF) on one platform for Latin American companies with a US entity.
product.problem_statement: Latin American founders incorporate in the US (mostly Delaware) and earn revenue in USD, but lack a physical address to open a US bank account. Existing fintechs focus on local-currency transactions or are stablecoin-centric, unsuitable for corporate cash management. Also, international transfers incur 4-5% FX fees.
product.solution: Open a USD business account remotely within 24 hours, with zero FX-margin international transfers, yield generation via T-bill MMFs (DSHXX, MULSX), and a 1.5% cashback Visa Infinite card. Also supports stablecoin transfers (USDC on Base, Ethereum, Polygon, Celo, Solana).
key_features: Remote US USD account opening (FDIC-insured, partner bank: Portage Bank)
Global transfers (US ACH/Wire, SEPA, Brazil Pix, Colombia Bre-B, and local rails in 15 countries)
Visa Infinite corporate card (0% foreign transaction fee, 1.5% cashback)
Short-term treasury: Dreyfus/Morgan Stanley MMF (not FDIC-insured)
Invoice issuance, vendor management, QuickBooks/Stripe integration for accounting automation
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: API integration with multiple banks and payment networks to manage cross-border cash flows from a single interface. Stablecoin transfer support provides an alternative to traditional banking.
product.target_customer: SME startups and mid-market companies with a US entity (mostly Delaware C-Corp) and team/customers/supply chain in Latin America.
product.business_model: Account maintenance fee (assumed free), international transfer fees (lower margins than competitors), card fees (interchange), and MMF management fees (partial).

direct_competitors.comparison: Banking for US startups. Unlike Blinka, mainly targets teams headquartered in the US, and has weak local transfer rails in Latin America.

omanta-2026.tagline: A healthcare company that runs a dedicated research lab for each patient.

founders.background: Experience in personalized vaccines, immuno-oncology, and radioligands. He was part of the bioinformatics team that assisted in the complete remission case of GitLab co-founder Sid Sijbrandij.
founders.notable_achievement: Contributed to the cancer cure case of GitLab co-founder Sid Sijbrandij (bioinformatics analysis)

founders.background: PhD in Chemical Biology from Harvard University. Experience at the Broad Institute and University of Pennsylvania. Co-founded and ran the Broad Institute Fellowship, leading a program to translate scientific discoveries into companies.
founders.notable_achievement: Identified a druggable mechanism for Ulcerative Colitis

omanta-2026.team_highlights: The two founders co-founded Omanta after working together on early CRISPR cancer research at the Broad Institute 8 years ago. Currently a lean team of 6 employees, with YC's Diana Hu serving as a batch partner.

product.summary: For patients with complex diseases who have exhausted standard treatment options, need recurrence preparation, or have unclear diagnoses, a dedicated research team of PhD-level scientists is assigned. The team integrates and analyzes medical records, genomics, imaging, pathology data, and existing research literature to interpret the patient's unique disease biology, providing a scientific direction and evidence roadmap that can be directly used by the attending physician to make clinical decisions.
product.problem_statement: Current healthcare has relied on average patient profiles, and individual cases where standard treatment doesn't work have been excluded from in-depth research opportunities. There has been no dedicated organization to continuously track the patient's complex biology and update scientific evidence.
product.solution: One dedicated research lab per patient manages the entire process: data collection and integration, identifying diagnostic gaps, coordinating additional tests, analyzing literature and clinical trials, and establishing treatment strategies. The output is not a one-time consultation but a continuously updated 'living roadmap'.
key_features: Dedicated research team of PhD scientists assigned
Integrated analysis of medical records, imaging, pathology, and molecular data
Coordination of additional diagnostic tests and support for tissue logistics
Literature and clinical trial analysis based on patient disease biology
Collaboration with the attending physician to connect scientific evidence to clinical decisions
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: Multidisciplinary approach including multi-omics data integration, natural language processing for record analysis, and exploring the possibility of personalized N-of-1 therapies. They have built a 'Research Lab as a Service' model combining proprietary analysis engines with operational infrastructure and personnel.
product.target_customer: Patients who have exhausted standard treatments, patients preparing for recurrence, and patients with undiagnosed diseases. The service is provided through collaboration with the attending physician (clinician) rather than directly to the patient, a B2B/B2C hybrid model.
product.business_model: Fee per patient case. Pricing is undisclosed, and insurance coverage has not yet been determined.

direct_competitors.comparison: A platform that ranks precision oncology treatment options, but unlike Omanta, it is not a service model with a dedicated science team operating over a long period.
Closer to a diagnostic kit offering genomic profiling. It competes at a different level than Omanta's comprehensive research service.
An academic research project attempting similar integrated analysis, but not yet commercialized.

competitive_landscape.key_differentiator: Rather than providing a software tool, it is a complete operational model where a PhD-level research team is 'dedicated' to a single patient, supporting logistics, data, experiments, literature analysis, and treatment strategy across the board.
competitive_landscape.moat: An operationally intensive structure deploying full-time research personnel per patient case. The unique capability to connect scientific rigor with clinical feasibility is difficult to replicate.
competitive_landscape.competitive_position_summary: An early-stage startup aiming to pioneer a unique category of 'personal dedicated research lab' in the market for complex diseases where standard diagnosis and treatment fail. Profitability and scalability still need to be proven.

trending_reason.summary: With participation in the Y Combinator 2026 Summer batch, the service officially launched in August 2026. Follow-up coverage by multiple outlets including Founderland.ai continued, and the unique approach of a 'lab for one patient' attracted attention in the precision medicine industry.

Forbes contributor Dasha Shunina's report in September 2026
GitLab co-founder Sid Sijbrandij's cancer recovery case draws attention as founding background
Growing industry interest in N-of-1 therapies and extreme precision medicine

atomarine-2026.tagline: Infrastructure startup building floating nuclear data centers at sea for the AI era.

founders.background: Graduated from MIT four times (BS/MS in EECS, MS in Mechanical Engineering, MBA). At Amazon, designed MILP optimization for EV charging, reducing CapEx by $193M. Managed portfolios at Arrowstreet Capital ($200B AUM).
founders.notable_achievement: Led Amazon's EV charging infrastructure optimization project.

founders.background: PhD in Nuclear Engineering, MS in Chemical Engineering. Graduated top of engineering at Ghent University, Fulbright scholar.
founders.notable_achievement: Holds a PhD in Nuclear Engineering.

atomarine-2026.team_highlights: Two MIT founders combine a Nuclear Engineering PhD (Chemical Engineering + Nuclear Engineering PhD) with a business/engineering background (EECS+MBA). Notably, CTO Germonpre holds a PhD in Nuclear Engineering, providing technical leadership in reactor technology.

product.summary: Atomarine builds infrastructure for operating AI data centers at sea using power ships equipped with small modular reactors (SMRs) mounted on standardized barges. Initially, it will run on natural gas turbines, with a plan to transition to SMRs by 2031-2032.
product.problem_statement: The surge in AI demand has led to skyrocketing data center power consumption, but on land, bottlenecks such as grid connection delays, community opposition, and shortages of water and land are severe. Additionally, securing power requires a 5-7 year wait.
product.solution: Move data centers 10-12 nautical miles offshore to operate independently without grid connection, achieve PUE <1.1 with seawater cooling. Mass-produce standardized barges at shipyards, cutting deployment time by 4x.
key_features: Separate power ship and compute barge design: only the power ship needs to be replaced to switch energy sources.
Seawater cooling eliminates freshwater consumption, PUE < 1.1.
Standardized 75-100MW compute barge production line.
Expandable to campus up to 450MW.
Initial natural gas, then SMR transition roadmap.
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: Design incorporating small modular reactors (SMRs) on power ships and standardized mass production of barges. Separating power and compute allows flexible response to technological evolution.
product.target_customer: Hyperscalers and AI companies with large-scale AI computing demand. Already secured over $4B in non-binding letters of intent (LOIs).
product.business_model: Builds and operates data center barges directly, leasing capacity or providing services on a capacity basis. Supplies power ships separately to sell fuel or electricity.

direct_competitors.comparison: Early pioneer of offshore data centers but focuses on water cooling without nuclear.
Develops subsea data centers but relies on onshore grid for power.
Wave and solar-powered offshore computing units, not nuclear or large-scale.

competitive_landscape.key_differentiator: Separating power ship and compute barge enables easy initial gas-to-nuclear transition, and standardized shipyard production maximizes scalability.
competitive_landscape.moat: Nuclear engineering PhD CTO + MIT network + Greek shipping industry connections + YC Summer 2026 batch + $4B in non-binding LOIs. However, SMR commercialization and regulatory approval are key challenges.
competitive_landscape.competitive_position_summary: One of the early leaders in the offshore data center market, and nearly unique with a nuclear-based solution. Large pre-orders exist, but it is not yet in the commercialization stage.

trending_reason.summary: The announcement of a $19M seed investment in November 2026 was the main trigger. As a YC Summer 2026 batch company, it is gaining attention amid surging AI infrastructure demand and expectations of SMR deregulation.
catalysts: 2025-2026 AI data center power demand surge.
Acceleration of SMR regulatory approval push.
YC Demo Day (August 2026) exposure.
trending_reason.growth_metrics: Secured KRW 400B in non-binding LOIs, targeting a gas-based pilot in 2028.

market_outlook.tam_sam_som: The global data center power market is estimated at about 100GW in 2026, growing 15-20% annually due to AI demand. Offshore data centers are in early stages but have a potential market of tens of billions of dollars.
market_outlook.market_trend: Offshore and nuclear data centers are emerging as alternatives to solve AI infrastructure expansion bottlenecks (power, land, cooling). As SMR regulation and commercialization approach, investment and attention are concentrating.
market_outlook.growth_potential: Explosive growth possible if SMR commercialization succeeds by 2030. In the short term, the success of the gas-based pilot is key.
risks: SMR commercialization and regulatory approval delays (no approved products in the US currently).
Technical challenges of offshore data center operations (waves, corrosion, maintenance).
Need for large initial capital investment (funding risk).
Increased competition from competitors (native offshore data centers, other SMR startups).
market_outlook.risk_mitigation: Market entry strategy with initial gas-based operations followed by SMR transition, cost reduction through standardized production with shipyard partnerships, and demand validation through non-binding LOIs.

atomarine-2026.editor_pick_comment: As the AI power crisis becomes real, the radical idea of offshore nuclear data centers has begun to move both investors and potential customers. The challenge for Atomarine is not technology but regulation and capital raising ability.

key_features: Embedded in containers and deployed on-site
Visual navigation-based response in GPS-denied environments

robocurve-2026.tagline: Independent evaluator of robot AI model performance

founders.background: Master's in Statistics from Harvard University, Bachelor's in Computer Science and Mathematics. MATS Research Fellow, Researcher at UK AI Safety Institute (AISI). Major contributor to Inspect Evals. Rhodes Scholar.
founders.notable_achievement: Accurately predicted all 50 state results in the 2024 U.S. presidential election.

robocurve-2026.team_highlights: Started as a 3-person core team, but now has contributions from over 200 university researchers and more than 30 open-source contributors.

product.summary: Robocurve is a Public Benefit Corporation that independently evaluates and benchmarks frontier AI models' ability to control real robots. Through its self-developed open-source evaluation framework, Inspect Robots, it can test the robot control performance of various AI models including LLMs, VLAs, and World Action Models (WAMs).
product.problem_statement: Currently, the AI industry relies on each lab evaluating robot capabilities on its own or depending on simulations. Without a standardized third-party robot benchmark, it's impossible to accurately compare the real performance of different models.
product.solution: Robocurve released Inspect Robots under the MIT license, enabling anyone to evaluate AI models' robot control capabilities under the same conditions. It also publishes regular evaluation results and funds benchmark development in academia.
key_features: Open-source MIT license
Supports various AI models including LLMs, VLAs, WAMs, and coding agents
Supports both real robots and simulation
Integrates with major robot platforms such as ROS and Isaac Lab
Provides full execution logs and real-time visualization
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: Python-based, extending Inspect AI for robot evaluation. Open-source with community contributions.
product.target_customer: Frontier AI labs (OpenAI, DeepMind, etc.), robot developers, government regulatory agencies, and academic researchers.
product.business_model: Specific revenue model not yet disclosed, but likely to generate revenue through premium evaluation services or enterprise reports. Operating as a Public Benefit Corporation signals prioritization of public interest over profitability.

direct_competitors.comparison: Robodojo also offers real robot evaluation suites, but Robocurve differentiates with its open-source framework and independence as a Public Benefit Corporation.

competitive_landscape.key_differentiator: Its legal status as an independent, neutral third-party evaluator, open-source approach, and academic collaboration are key differentiators.
competitive_landscape.moat: Rapid open-source community adoption (6M+ views, 97K+ downloads, 200+ registered institutions), first-mover advantage, and trust relationships with frontier labs.
competitive_landscape.competitive_position_summary: As the first to secure large-scale funding and community in robot AI evaluation, it is a frontrunner with high potential to become the standard.

trending_reason.summary: In September 2026, it raised a $10M seed round led by Initialized Capital, and in November released the first stable version of its evaluation framework. As AI applications in the physical world accelerate, demand for independent evaluation is growing.
catalysts: Frontier AI labs' general-purpose robot goals (2028)
Increasing social and political pressure for AI safety and transparency
Y Combinator participation and heightened visibility
Virtual absence of a robot evaluation infrastructure market
trending_reason.growth_metrics: 6M+ views on research content, 97K+ downloads of Inspect Robots, participation from 200+ universities and research institutions in benchmarks, 30+ open-source contributors.

latest_round.note: Officially announced September 14, 2026

funding_history.note: First institutional investment after joining YC Summer 2026 batch

market_outlook.tam_sam_som: The global AI safety evaluation market is still nascent, making it difficult to estimate its exact size. However, if robot evaluation becomes an industry standard, it could grow from tens of billions to hundreds of billions of KRW.
market_outlook.market_trend: As AI models' application in the physical world expands, the need for evaluation infrastructure is exploding.
market_outlook.growth_potential: Very high. Since the robot evaluation market is virtually non-existent, rapid market share capture is possible.
risks: Frontier AI labs could strengthen their own evaluation tools or introduce proprietary evaluations
Potential fragmentation of standards due to open-source project divergence
Regulatory uncertainty
market_outlook.risk_mitigation: Strategy of legally ensuring independence and neutrality, and expanding the ecosystem through open-source collaboration with academia.
